Connor / team — quick model shortlist and sizing notes below based on the token profile and the use case. Numbers are conservative; I included assumptions so the CS team can validate with procurement.

Assumptions used (from lumen_token_profile_v1.xlsx):
- 60k unique patients/month -> 60k sessions/month
- Avg messages per session: 3 (user prompts + assistant replies) -> ~9 message-level calls per session
- Average session tokens: 350 (prompt + completion), tail up to 2,000 tokens for long histories
- We estimate 20% of sessions will hit the long-history path requiring 2k-token context processing.

Shortlist (ranked):
1) OpenRed-XL-8B (quality-priority)
   - Recommended context window: 2,048 tokens native; use sliding-summary for histories >2k
   - Quantization: q4_0 recommended on Dedicated for cost savings with minimal quality loss
   - Estimated p95 token latency: 18ms/token on a single A100-class GPU equivalent
   - Pilot token cost estimate (hosted pricing heuristic): ~45M tokens/month -> cost ballpark $3.2k–$6k depending on variant and batching

2) RedOpt-3B (latency-cost optimized)
   - Context window: 1,024 tokens; suggest prompt engineering to trim older context and summarize
   - Quantization: q8_0 for max throughput on Dedicated pools
   - p95 token latency: 9ms/token
   - Pilot tokens: ~45M tokens/month -> cost ballpark $1.1k–$2k

3) MedSpec-7B (specialized medical safety-tuned)
   - Context window: 2,560 tokens (benefit for longer histories)
   - Quantization: mixed precision recommended; require compatibility testing in staging
   - p95 token latency: 22ms/token
   - Pilot tokens: ~$4k–$8k depending on hosting and quantization

4) TinyStream-1.3B (compact fallback for burst/low-cost routing)
   - Context window: 512 tokens; good for quick triage steps only
   - p95 token latency: 5ms/token
   - Use as overflow route for cost control
Recommendations on context strategy:
- For triage assistant, preserve full recent history up to 2k tokens. For sessions that grow beyond that, run a light summarization pass (1k token summary) and store summary in KV cache. This balances accuracy with cost.
- Use prefix caching for repeated system instructions and patient metadata to avoid re-tokenizing static context.

Token volume estimate methodology (short):
- Total monthly tokens = sessions * avg tokens per session * messages per session
- With 60k sessions, 350 tokens/session, 9 calls -> rough total tokens processed ~189M tokens/month. (This is an upper-bound; batching and prefix caching typically reduce Billable tokens by ~20–35% depending on traffic shape.)

Notes for CS / Dedicated sizing:
- For peak concurrent 120 sessions with median response sizes, a small Dedicated pool (2x A100-equivalent GPUs) with autoscale burst to 4 GPUs should cover pilot latency SLOs if using RedOpt-3B or OpenRed-XL with batching tuned.
- If customer insists on storing full 2k histories per request without summarization, capacity needs jump ~2.5x and cost increases accordingly.

Next steps I recommend:
- Short internal call (30 min) to validate assumptions and finalize pilot token estimate (Connor + Anya + Rajiv + Marissa + Monica).
- Run a 2-day perf test in staging with 10k synthetic sessions to validate latency and token billing profile.

I can attach a more detailed spreadsheet of the cost math if useful.
